ideas.title: Lay the plank road yourself: planks are bodies, the cart thumps over your seams
ideas.critique: This is the first time the cart is judged by something the player made: dropped planks settle by contact, and a badly laid road makes the cart thump and see-saw because the contact decides, not because a script does. That is a real step past a cart rolling on a road nobody built. The risk is in the wheels. Affine bodies on revolute joints rolling under IPC friction is the hard part, and if the wheels end up driven kinematically and only the planks are simulated, it shrinks back into the cord film with bumps added.

ideas.title: Wind the coil by hand, the wire laid by its own tension
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This fixes what round 1's beak winding lacked: turns land where tension, the guide and contact put them, and the motor answers with the ampere-turns and resistance of the player's own coil. That is a hand skill with a solved payoff, and it builds the part the motor needs. Two hundred turns of a contact rod against itself is expensive, and the side-by-side 'neat vs sloppy' film is the old variants-compared shape. If the turn count is ever read off a script instead of off the rod, or the beak slides on the crank, nothing is left of the idea.

ideas.title: Stir the brine: a solved flow thins the tired layer
ideas.critique: This answers round 1's complaint about a reset switch with a real advected concentration field, and seeing the green smear off the bar under your stick is a nice piece of visible electrochemistry. But a horizontal 2D slice cannot show the still vertical layer the sag comes from, and the film is once more dusk jars that pay off as a cart going further. Stirring pots to win volts back is upkeep, not a choice with much depth.
